title: Phone: Mesabi Taconite Works Calls Again: "Is It Getting Worse?"

fields.systemName: Recorded Line - Primary Control Room, Customer Line

callee.name: Walter Nakamura
callee.label: Control Room Shift Supervisor, NLTO Duluth

transcript.speaker: NLTO
transcript.text: NLTO control room, this is the shift supervisor.

transcript.speaker: Mesabi
transcript.text: Yeah, it's Peter Lindgren at Mesabi again. Look, my electrician says our 115 kV voltage blinked at sixteen-twenty. Just a blink, but the drives on Line 2 noticed it. And somebody out here heard a big line at Hartley went down. Is that true?

transcript.speaker: Mesabi
transcript.text: Okay. Here's my problem. The plant manager is standing in my doorway and he wants a straight answer in the next fifteen minutes. Do I shut the indurating furnace now, while I can do it controlled, or do I ride it out?

transcript.speaker: Mesabi
transcript.text: Because if I take ninety megawatts off and you black me out anyway, I've lost a day of pellets for nothing. And if I don't, and the furnace trips cold, that's eight hours before I make product again. So I need to know which way this is going.

transcript.speaker: Mesabi
transcript.text: You told me this morning you'd keep me posted, and I haven't heard from anybody since. So... is it getting worse? Yes or no?

voiceStyles.NLTO: Calm control room supervisor, mid-40s, phones and alarm chimes faintly behind
voiceStyles.Mesabi: Man in his 50s, Iron Range accent, polite but clipped and under pressure, plant noise and a radio in the background, speaks faster as the call goes on

instructorNote: This call adds friction: the shift has to give a large customer facts during the 345-1 trip and G4 conditions without promising anything or making the furnace decision for him. Watch whether the TOM or CRSS tells Mesabi about Condition 4, G4, the open Hartley–Iron Range 345-1 line and that no customer load has been lost, then asks Mesabi to keep its power factor correction in service and to call NLTO before any 90 MW load change, and logs the call.

voiceLines.text: Because if I take ninety megawatts off and you black me out anyway, I've lost a day of pellets for nothing. And if I don't, and the furnace trips cold, that's eight hours before I make product again. So I need to know which way this is going.
